title: Understanding Data Drift and Concept Drift in Machine Learning Systems
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology
tldr: Comprehensive examination of data drift and concept drift challenges in production ML systems, with analysis of detection methodologies and mitigation strategies across healthcare, manufacturing, autonomous systems, and edge computing.
problem_and_motivation: Production machine learning models experience significant performance degradation due to the continuous evolution of data patterns over time, a phenomenon known as drift. This drift affects approximately 92% of production ML systems within their first 18 months, leading to average performance degradation of 31.7%. The problem is particularly critical in healthcare, where undetected drift in risk assessment models led to a 34% increase in false negatives.
approach: Comprehensive literature review of drift detection methodologies including statistical approaches (KS test, JSD, PSI) and concept drift detection methods (DDM, Page Hinkley, ADWIN).
Analysis of drift manifestations across multiple domains: healthcare medical imaging, manufacturing processes, autonomous driving systems, and maritime sensor networks.
Synthesis of findings from real-world implementations across 215 healthcare organizations, 78 manufacturing facilities, and 12 autonomous driving datasets.
Evaluation of mitigation strategies including model adaptation, advanced retraining methodologies, ensemble-based solutions, and infrastructure monitoring.
Examination of future developments in sustainable manufacturing drift detection with energy-aware systems.
Integration of findings across multiple papers to present a holistic view of drift management challenges and solutions.
findings: num: Undetected drift leads to average performance degradation of 31.7% in model accuracy.
num: Healthcare applications experience degradation rates up to 52% within the first year of deployment.
num: Demographic shifts in patient populations resulted in a 23.4% decrease in diagnostic accuracy over eight months.
num: Early drift detection can reduce model degradation by up to 83.5%.
num: Models deployed in clinical settings require recalibration approximately every 3.5 months.
num: Sensor data distributions can shift up to 47.2% due to equipment wear and environmental variations.
num: KS-test-based monitoring systems identified 91.3% of significant distribution changes in autonomous driving data within 18 milliseconds.
num: ADWIN-based monitoring detected concept drift with 89.4% accuracy in edge computing environments.
num: Implementing energy-aware retraining systems reduced model degradation by 76.8% while decreasing carbon footprint by 52.4%.
num: Manufacturing facilities implementing structured impact evaluation protocols reported a 58.9% improvement in model stability over 18 months.

definitions.definition: A fundamental shift in the statistical properties of input features over time.
The evolution of relationships between input features and target variables over time.
A type of data drift where input feature distributions change while underlying relationships remain stable.
A type of data drift where target variable distributions change, often due to process improvements or material variations.
Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, a non-parametric approach for detecting distribution shifts in data streams.
Jensen-Shannon Divergence, a method for comparing probability distributions in perception systems.
Population Stability Index, a metric for monitoring distribution stability across systems.
Drift Detection Method, an approach for identifying sudden concept shifts with minimal computational resources.
Adaptive Windowing, an approach for detecting concept drift with dynamic window sizing.
Overall Equipment Effectiveness, a manufacturing metric impacted by concept drift.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides a comprehensive synthesis of drift detection and mitigation challenges across multiple domains, offering quantitative evidence of performance degradation in production ML systems. It systematically evaluates various detection methodologies and presents comparative performance metrics across different application contexts. The paper bridges theoretical drift concepts with practical implementation considerations, particularly in resource-constrained environments like edge computing. The examination of sustainable manufacturing applications contributes to the growing literature on energy-aware ML systems. The work establishes baseline performance expectations and detection latencies that can inform future research on adaptive ML systems.

topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains revealed that this paper primarily contributes to ML system monitoring and evaluation frameworks rather than personal finance-specific topics. The paper's content on drift detection evaluation methodologies maps directly to Topic 12.A (Evaluation Frameworks) and 12.B (Evaluation of Algorithmic Modules) with high relevance due to the comprehensive comparative analysis of detection methods. Topic 6.A (Predictive Modeling) and 8.A (Anomaly Detection) were assigned contextual relevance as the paper provides foundational concepts applicable to these areas but does not address personal finance applications. Topics related to Filipino young professionals, financial structures, spending patterns, and budgeting strategies were considered and rejected as the paper contains no content specific to personal finance systems or user financial behavior. Topics 10.A and 10.B were assigned contextual relevance due to the discussion of healthcare data privacy and system reliability. The overall topical coverage is focused on ML system drift management with strong relevance to evaluation and algorithmic assessment domains, and limited direct relevance to personal finance-specific topics.
